subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw define and own a stable runtime-neutral agent-core protocol for no-Node and bare-metal ports, or should embedded/MimiClaw-style runtimes remain external ports that only consume existing OpenClaw concepts?
rationale: Current code and docs still require a Node-hosted OpenClaw runtime, and creating a C/Rust/WASM/bare-metal contract would set a long-lived architecture and ownership boundary that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Keep canonical RFC/design issue
options.body: Use this issue for maintainer-sponsored protocol design, conformance tests, and core-versus-external ownership decisions before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to plugin/API work
options.body: Treat near-term language-agnostic work as plugin SDK or JSON-RPC ABI work, leaving full no-Node runtime ports outside this issue until the core protocol is approved.

options.title: Mark not planned for core
options.body: Close the issue only if maintainers decide OpenClaw will stay Node/TypeScript-hosted and MimiClaw-style ports should remain independent projects.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical RFC/design issue
recommendation.body: Use this issue for maintainer-sponsored protocol design, conformance tests, and core-versus-external ownership decisions before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current signal for runtime/platform boundary history and already participated in this issue's keep-open review.
